note: Plain-language requirements a software team writes, and the GDPR articles a reviewer would open for each. Written by the project (AI-assisted) before any search was run on them; several articles can be right. It measures ranking on the real text, not legal correctness.

cases.statement: Users can delete their account and all their data
Users can download a copy of everything we store about them
Users can export their data as JSON to move to another service
Users can correct a wrong date of birth in their profile
We ask permission before sending marketing emails and users can take it back any time
Children under 16 need a parent's approval to sign up
We tell the authority within three days when customer records leak
We email affected customers when their passwords are stolen
Passwords are hashed and the database is encrypted at rest
We only collect the fields we actually need for signup
Old inactive accounts are purged after two years
The privacy page explains what we collect and why when users register
Our hosting provider signs an agreement to handle data only on our instructions
We keep a register of all our data handling with purposes and recipients
Before launching face recognition login we assess the risks to users
Loan applications are never rejected purely by an algorithm without a human looking
Users can opt out of profiling for personalised ads
We store health information only with the user's explicit agreement
Customer data sent to our US analytics vendor is covered by standard contract clauses
We appoint a privacy officer because we monitor users at large scale
New features default to the most private settings
Users can pause use of their data while a complaint about its accuracy is checked
When a user corrects or deletes data we pass that on to partners who received it
We have a representative in the EU since our company is based outside it
Staff with database access act only on our instructions
We answer data requests within one month and free of charge
We can show records proving that we follow the rules
We bought an email list and must tell those people where we got their details
Handling the order is necessary to deliver what the customer bought
Users can complain to the regulator
Two companies together decide how the shared customer database is used and agree who does what
We consult the regulator when an assessment shows a high risk we cannot reduce
Criminal record checks on drivers happen only where the law allows
The rules cover our Berlin office even though the servers are in Singapore
Fines can reach four percent of worldwide turnover
Our subcontractor tells us without delay when it discovers a leak
Users are told the logic behind automated credit scoring
Data collected for billing is not reused for advertising
A user who objects to direct marketing stops receiving it
People harmed by misuse of their data can claim compensation
